subject: Warm standby switchover tolerance — activation window & RTO/RPO exceptions
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cardinalbank.eu>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: security@cardinalbank.eu
Date: Mon, 12 Aug 2029 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Warm standby — EU regulatory activation window requirement

Hi Mateo,

Following up from our compliance review: Cardinal is required by local regulators to be able to bring production-critical services online within 45 minutes of a regional failure (RTO <= 45 minutes) and to limit data loss to 15 minutes (RPO <= 15m) for services affecting EU customers.

Your standard warm-standby activation guidance (2h lead time) won't meet that requirement. We need Redwood to commit to an amended SLA for our eu-west region that guarantees: 
- RTO: 45 minutes or less from detection to traffic switch or a documented failover path that achieves the equivalent for customer-facing endpoints
- RPO: 15 minutes or less for token-level persisted sessions and KV caches

Please confirm whether Redwood can provide a carve-out/addendum for Cardinal, or whether we need a dedicated standby pool (and the cost/terms for that). Attaching the regulator notice for context.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachment: Cardinal_regulatory_notice.pdf (pdf, 210KB)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cardinalbank.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Aug 2029 09:20:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Warm standby — EU regulatory activation window requirement

Hi Elena — thanks for the detail and attaching the notice. We take regulatory SLAs seriously and want to be helpful here. High level: it is possible to meet the RTO/RPO you describe, but it requires changes to the standing configuration and an operational commitment we typically surface as an SLA addendum.

Options we can offer (summary):
1) Priority warm standby (recommended for Cardinal) — pre-warmed, reserved capacity in eu-west with a hot KV-sync lane: cost: +monthly reserved charge; impact: can achieve RTO <= 45m, RPO <= 15m.
2) Dedicated hot-standby — full dedicated replica that eliminates most activation steps: higher cost but lowest risk; RTO < 30m.
3) Standard shared warm standby with runbook integration — we can shorten lead time to 60 minutes under a runbook and an automated routing policy, but 45m is only achievable for limited flows and not guaranteed.

Proposed next steps to get to an actionable SLA addendum:
- We’ll draft a tailored amendment that specifies the warm-standby priority configuration, activation playbook, test cadence, and service credits tied to missed RTO/RPO windows.
- We require a 30-day pilot (activation drills) before the SLA becomes effective to verify telemetry and handoffs.
- Additional requirements: SOC2 report, KMS key agreement, and a brief vendor risk attestation (attached).

If you want the firm 45m RTO guarantee, we recommend Option 1 with the reserved pre-warmed pool. I attached a draft amendment; it includes pricing and the proposed service-credit table (3x reduction in monthly service credits if pre-warm not provisioned).

Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the architecture and pricing?

Thanks — Mateo

Attachment: proposed-sla-amendment.pdf (pdf, 78KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cardinalbank.eu>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Aug 2029 14:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Warm standby — EU regulatory activation window requirement

Elena / Mateo — looping in the compliance side to document the gating items so legal can prepare an addendum quickly. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 45m RTO guarantee is operationally achievable only if we have a pre-warmed reserved capacity with automatic KV sync and a prioritized routing policy for Cardinal traffic. That is what Mateo called "Priority warm standby."
- To accept the SLA carve-out we require:
  * Current SOC2 Type II report (within last 12 months)
  * Completed vendor risk questionnaire (attached)
  * KMS key escrow or approved customer-managed KMS config
  * Quarterly activation drills documented in the amendment

Proposed acceptance path:
1) Cardinal signs the SLA addendum and vendor risk form.
2) Redwood provisions the reserved pool and performs three activation drills during a 30-day pilot.
3) If all drills meet the RTO/RPO thresholds, the addendum becomes effective on the date of the final drill report.

If Cardinal needs a faster path to an effective date, Option 2 (Dedicated hot-standby) shortens verification but will be priced as a dedicated replica.

I attached the vendor risk questionnaire — please return filled. We can review answers on the call.

— Kimberly

Attachment: vendor-risk-questionnaire.docx (docx, 45KB)

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@cardinalbank.eu>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Aug 2029 16:20:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Warm standby — EU regulatory activation window requirement

Thanks, Mateo / Kimberly. We reviewed internally and would like to proceed with Option 1 (Priority warm standby) under the conditions you outlined. A couple of small asks before we sign: 

1) Add a single mandatory full activation (end-to-end) stress test within the first 45 days with reportable metrics.
2) Slightly revise the service-credit table so that missed RTO windows (single event) yield a minimum 5% monthly credit rather than the 3% in the draft.

We will return the completed vendor risk questionnaire and attach our SOC2 summary. Can you confirm final pricing for the reserved pool and send a clean signature page for the addendum?

I'll attach the signed vendor acceptance once legal signs off.

Best,
Elena

Attachment: signed-amendment.pdf (pdf, 12KB)
